provenance: Bodies that must appear in the roster whatever the split search ranks. Applied AFTER `enumerate_splits.py`, so the search never overwrites them. Each entry is keyed by build address — `<class>/<subclass heading>:<niche>` — and is merged into `chassis-seeds.json` as an ordinary build, then scored like any other. Forcing decides only the split; it does not exempt a body from scoring, crosscheck or the promotion bar.
why_this_file_exists: The split search cannot express a three-class body whose dips both name a subclass. `dip_sets` offers only generic parts once a split has two dip classes, so `Ranger 15 / Fighter 2 / Barbarian 3` is reachable and `Ranger 15 / Monk 3 (Way of the Friar) / Cleric 2 (Light)` is not, even though both parts are catalogued. Lifting that restriction means enumerating the cross product of both dips' subclass lists, which is roughly a hundredfold on the affected cells. Forcing the handful of bodies that matter is cheaper than widening the search, and it keeps the search's output honest about what it actually explored.

ranger/Snowlight Conclave:reaction.split: Ranger 15 (Snowlight Conclave) / Monk 3 (Way of the Friar) / Cleric 2 (Light)
ranger/Snowlight Conclave:reaction.why: Friar's Retribution converts every incoming hit into Radiant, which Glaring Frost turns into a blind save and Anthelion spreads to the cluster.
ranger/Snowlight Conclave:reaction.note: Niched `reaction` rather than `lockdown` because the sweep's own Snowlight body, Whiteout, already holds lockdown with a Paladin smite dip, and the two are genuinely different bodies. The niche also reads true: the engine is `OnAttacked`, the Kin half is an interrupt spending Lone Wolf's second reaction, and the brief's own gloss on `reaction` is `needs a build shaped around being attacked`.
